BURHAN:v4p299/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p299/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p299/r3.claim: The missing fa after إذا has three explanations: إذا is temporal rather than conditional, هم is emphatic, or the fa is omitted because the verb is past; the first also explains the clause beginning وإذا تتلى.
BURHAN:v4p299/r3.anchor: فإن قيل فلم سقطت الفاء في قوله ﴿ وإذا ما غضبوا هم يغفرون ﴾ 2 قلنا عنه ثلاثة أجوبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r3.claim: God questions the condemned through whichever angels He wills; “My signs” means the Qurʾān.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r3.anchor: يقول الله لهم على لسان من يشاء من ملائكته ألم تكن آياتي وهي القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r6.claim: The signs recited to them mean the Qur’an, by which they were warned.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r6.anchor: يعني القرآن، تخوفون بها، {فكنتم بها تكذبون}

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r4.claim: The question about God's signs is spoken to them with an implied speech verb and reminds them of the reason for their punishment: denial.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r4.anchor: على إضمار القول أي يقال لهم { ألم تكن }

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r4.claim: The question about God's signs has an omitted introduction, namely that it is said to them; the signs here are the Quran.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r4.anchor: وقوله ألم تكن آياتي قبله محذوف تقديره يقال لهم، و «الآيات» هنا القرآن

MUQATIL:23:101-105/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r6.claim: The unbelievers are reminded that the Quran was recited to them about the Day and what would happen, but they denied it.
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r6.anchor: يقول: ألم يكن القرآن يقرأ عليكم فى أمر هذا اليوم، وما هو كائن فيكم،

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r17.claim: The condemned are reproached because God's clear signs were recited to them but they denied them, making them deserve the painful punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r17.anchor: فلا جرم صرتم مستحقين لما أنتم فيه من العذاب الأليم

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r18.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r18.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that the verse assigns punishment to bad deeds, which would be unjust if God created human acts.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r18.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : الآية تدل على أنهم

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r19.claim: Al-Razi answers that an unmotivated sin would be accidental, not voluntary, and so could not merit punishment; if motivated, its cause was not the person's act without an infinite regress, making the resulting act compelled and undeserving of reward.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r19.anchor: إن صدرت المعصية عنه لا لمرجح ألبتة كان صدورها عنه اتفاقيا لا اختياريا

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.claim: The conclusion warns that disbelievers facing their perdition will wish to return to do good instead of evil, but it will be too late.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.anchor: will desire to go back to the world in order to do good instead of evil, though it will be too late for them (vv.99–118)

TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r5.claim: The question about God's signs means they will be asked whether the signs were recited to them and they denied them.
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r5.anchor: أي يقال لهم ألم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم فكنتم بها تكذبون

TABRISI:23:101-108/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101-108/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:101-108/r13.claim: The rebuke asks whether the Quran, or God’s proofs and arguments, had not been recited to them in worldly life.
TABRISI:23:101-108/r13.anchor: ألم تكن حججي وبيناتي وأدلتي تقرأ عليكم في دار الدنيا

ASAD-NOTES:23:105/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:105/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:105/r1.claim: God asks the condemned whether His messages had been conveyed to them and whether they habitually denied them.
ASAD-NOTES:23:105/r1.anchor: Were not My messages conveyed unto you, and were you [not] wont to give them the lie?

ALUSI-FULL:v18p67/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67/r1.claim: An implicit يقال لهم introduces the question as rebuke and reminder of why they deserve punishment: God's signs were recited to them in worldly life, and they denied them.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67/r1.anchor: على إضمار القول أي يقال لهم تعنيفا وتوبيخا وتذكيرا لما به استحقوا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r1.claim: The question is a rebuke spoken to the punished: God’s signs had been recited to them in worldly life, but they persisted in denying them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r1.anchor: أي يقال لهم في تأنيبهم وتوبيخهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r2.claim: The signs are described as reaching the highest rank because they are attributed to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r2.anchor: التي انتهى عظمها إلى أعلى المراتب بإضافتها إلي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r3.claim: The passive construction highlights that the signs’ mere recitation should have sufficed for belief.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r4.claim: Putting “in them” before “you denied” emphasizes how persistently they rejected the signs that should have led them to faith.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r4.anchor: قدم الظرف للإعلام بمبالغتهم في التكذيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r1.claim: The question is part of an omitted speech addressed to the condemned on that Day: they are asked whether God’s signs were recited to them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r1.anchor: مقول قول محذوف ، أي يقال لهم يومئذ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r2.claim: The signs are Qur’anic verses, as indicated by the verbs ‘recited to you’ and ‘you denied them’ in their ordinary senses.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r3.claim: تلاوة means reading or recitation; Ibn Ashur cites prior usage in al-Baqara and al-Anfal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r3.anchor: والتلاوة : القراءة . وقد تقدم عند قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r4.claim: The question is reproachful and denies their excuse.

BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r1.claim: God’s signs were recited to them in worldly life, and they denied them then.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492/r1.claim: They are being told: were My signs, meaning the Quran, not recited to you?
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى الم تكن المعنى ويقال لهم الم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم يعني القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p498/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p498/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p498/r1.claim: God rebukes and reproaches the people of Hell for the disbelief, sins, forbidden acts, and grave offenses that ruined them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p498/r1.anchor: هذا تقريع من الله تعالى لأهل النار، وتوبيخ لهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p498/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p498/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p498/r2.claim: God sent messengers and books and removed their objections, leaving no excuse; Ibn Kathir links this to passages denying punishment before a messenger and recounting Hell's inmates admitting they rejected warning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p498/r2.anchor: قد أرسلت إليكم الرسل، وأنزلت الكتب، وأزلت

NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#5/r1.claim: God’s signs here are the Quran, recited to them in worldly life; they denied it and claimed it was not from God.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ ألم تكن آياتي ﴾ أى القرآن ﴿ تتلى عليكم ﴾ فى الدنيا ﴿ فكنتم بها تكذبون ﴾

RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r1.claim: After God asks whether His signs were recited while they denied them, the condemned answer with two explanations.
RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r1.anchor: ذكروا ما يجري مجرى الجواب عنه وهو من وجهين

TAB-FULL:v17p116/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī identifies the rebuke as Qur'anic verses recited and rejected in worldly life, then the sinners answer in the Hell scene by saying decreed wretchedness overcame them.
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r1.anchor: قال ابن جريج: بلغنا " أن أهل النار نادوا خزنة جهنم: أن {ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب} [غافر: 49]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the recited signs as warnings given to them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: ألم تخوفوا بها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73/r2.claim: In worldly life they denied the Qur'an and Muhammad concerning the Fire and its punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73/r2.anchor: فكنتم في الدنيا تكذبون القرآن ومحمدا -عليه السلام- بالنار وعذابها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r1.claim: This question is put to the people while they are in Hell.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r1.claim: At the afterlife judgment, God reminds the disbelievers that they denied His recited revelations; this sin is singled out because their other evils began with that rejection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r1.anchor: Allah inkârcılara, âyetleri kendilerine okunduğunda onları yalanlayıp reddettiklerini hatırlatır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r4.claim: Their plea to be brought out will go unanswered because they should have made it during worldly life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r4.anchor: “Bizi buradan çıkar!” feryatları da karşılıksız kalacaktır. Çünkü bu yakarışları dünyada yapmaları gerekirdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r5.claim: In worldly life, sincere Muslims prayed and prepared for salvation while disbelievers mocked them; now the believers have attained the happy outcome.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r5.anchor: o inkârcılar bu günahsız müminleri küçümseyip alaya alıyorlardı. Ama şimdi mutlu âkıbeti o müminler elde etmişlerdir

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r7.claim: Āyāt can mean God’s books, which are recited to people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r7.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الآية في القرآن على ستة أوجه : -

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r7.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r7.claim: The signs in the next verse are the Qurʾān.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r3.claim: They are confronted with the fact that God’s signs were recited to them and they denied them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r3.anchor: ألم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم فكنتم بها تكذبون

BURHAN:v1p407#2/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p407#2/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p407#2/r6.claim: The nūn remains in ألم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم because the act of reciting the signs has reached completion.
BURHAN:v1p407#2/r6.anchor: فإن كون تلاوة الآيات قد أكمل كونه وتم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r14.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r14.speaker: الزركشي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r14.claim: Al-Zarkashi contrasts these with incomplete beginnings: the recitation of the signs and the earth’s being spacious are already fully realized states, so their forms retain nūn.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r14.anchor: فإن كون تلاوة الآيات قد أكمل كونه وتَمَّ. وكذلك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p650/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p650/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p650/r3.claim: The nūn remains in references to God's spacious earth and recited signs because each is fully specified and the meaning is complete.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p650/r3.anchor: لم تحذف النون من الفعل هنا لأن الآيات مكتملة والأرض مكتملة فجاء بالفعل تامّاً لأن المعنى تامّ
